newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends down sharply in a correction.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends down sharply in a correction.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices pulled back sharply on Wednesday as speculators took profits following two straight sessions of gains, traders said.
"It was just a correction," one trader said. "Some technical profit taking rather than anything else."
Prices bounced on either side of unchanged for much of the session, but the market slid toward session lows late amid heavy long liquidation.
Most-active May ended down 7.05 cents at 196.10 cents a lb after trading from 205.50 to 195.00. Spot March closed 3.35 cents lower at 215.65 cents, while the rest finished unchanged to down 5.20.
Traders said active May's failure to get past near-term resistance at 205.50 cents inspired the bout of profit taking.
"For two successive days it failed to get past 205.50," said Refco In analyst Ann Prendergast, "and locals and specs took profits."
However, Prendergast said the widening of the nearby March/May switch to 19.55 cents from 15.85 cents Tuesday could be seen as a buy signal.
Traders brushed aside news that Colombia's largest truck drivers' association is preparing its second nationwide stoppage in five months.
"All this Colombian situation is in the market," one trader said. "They settled strikes and the market should have gone down but it kept making new highs."
The Colombian Truckers' Association (ACC) will set the start date for the strike at a meeting on March 22, one of the organization's senior officials told Reuters this week.
Technically, PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko said today's outside range day -- surpassing Tuesday's high but closing beneath its low -- could weigh on sentiment.
"The real test is if May can trade below Monday's low of 185.20," Savaiko said, adding a break of that level may confirm that the recent rally was over.

After Wednesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks grew for the fifth day in a row, reaching 38,083 60-kg bags as of March 11. There were an additional 14,246 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
With less than a week left to go before the spot March contract goes off the board, its open interest was still relatively high at 1,003 lots -- or the equivalent of more than 250,000 bags of coffee.

Also after the close, Maxwell House Coffee Co said it revised its increase on the list price of its standard 13-ounce can of coffee to 60 cents from the 45-cent increase announced Feb 21, due to the price of green coffee on the world's futures markets, the company said.
The increase, which takes effect March 31, brings the price for a standard can to $2.86, the Maxwell House said.
Today's turnover was estimated at 10,413 lots, compared with Tuesday's official tally of 12,061 lots. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk +1 212 859 1640))
